title: Maximal ideal and structural map in an affine strict-henselization chart
statement: Let S be a scheme, Ω an algebraically closed field, R a commutative ring, i : Spec R → S an open immersion and xR : Spec Ω → Spec R. Put s = xR followed by i and C = [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], the coordinate ring of S_(s). There exist a local-ring structure on C and a ring map ρ : R → C such that Spec(ρ) followed by i is [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map] and the maximal ideal of C is the extension under ρ of the prime xR(closedPoint Ω).

source.place: Tag 04HX, affine-chart colimit identification; Tag 04GW, triple colimit; Tag 04GP, property (4). Sources read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04HX, /04GW and /04GP.

proof.text: Apply etale_local_ring_triples to the affine open i and geometric point xR. It supplies the chart restriction, the equivalence E with residue triples, the natural diagram isomorphism δ, and compatible colimit cocones cn and ct. Apply strictHenselization_triples with the relative separable closure to obtain a local colimit c, its R-map ρ, and maximalIdeal(c) = p.map(ρ).

The inverse small-model equivalence followed by strictHenselizationAffineInclusion is an equivalence q. The final-functor colimit isomorphism for q, the comparison with cn, the chart-to-triples comparison and uniqueness of the triple colimit yield ringIso : strictHenselizationRing(xR ≫ i) ≅ c.pt. Transport locality by the inverse ring equivalence and use ρ ≫ ringIso.inv as the R-map.

Choose a representative j isomorphic to the pointed chart (Spec R,xR). Its affine image b has a map g to Spec R. Coprojection formulas for all colimit comparisons and the equation (ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ g.appTop ≫ δ = the triple R-map give (ΓSpecIso R).inv ≫ g.appTop ≫ colimit.ι(j) = ρ ≫ ringIso.inv. Apply Spec and naturality of isoSpec.inv, and compose with i. Since g ≫ i is the neighbourhood structure map, its structural-map coprojection equation gives Spec.map(ρ ≫ ringIso.inv) ≫ i = strictHenselizationStructuralMap(xR ≫ i).

Ring equivalences carry maximal ideals to maximal ideals. Map maximalIdeal(c) = p.map(ρ) through ringIso.inv and use Ideal.map_map to get the required ideal identity. The point p in SpecToEquivOfField equals xR(closedPoint Ω).

lean.statement: theorem strictHenselization_chart_maximalIdeal {S : Scheme.{u}} {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (R : CommRingCat.{u}) (i : Spec R ⟶ S) [IsOpenImmersion i] (xR : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Spec R) : ∃ (_ : IsLocalRing (strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i))) (ρ : R ⟶ strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i)), Spec.map ρ ≫ i = strictHenselizationStructuralMap (xR ≫ i) ∧ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (strictHenselizationRing (xR ≫ i)) = (xR (IsLocalRing.closedPoint Ω)).asIdeal.map ρ.hom
